Commentary.Commentary: So, that is it from this game. South Africa have sealed the series with a game left. Do join us for the third ODI which will be played on the 6th of October in Paarl at 1300 local (1100 GMT). Till then goodbye and take care!

South Africa skipper, JP Duminy, says the pitch was not an ideal one. Further adds the pitches here are normally flat. Mentions it was a good effort by the lower order to take them close to 200. States they needed wickets up front and they got them. Reckons the players have not yet stepped up to the opportunity but they have the third ODI to prove themselves and stake a claim in the World Cup squad. Credits Tahir for the way he bowled. Ends by saying they are looking forward to the third game and he hopes the guys who are getting the opportunity will grab it with both hands.

Man of the Match, Dale Steyn, says the wicket was quite tough but playing the spinners was easier compared to the pacers. Further adds he built a partnership with Phehlukwayo and they did well. He feels good entering this game after playing quite a few county games. Reckons the wicket was a little up and down and he would not mind bowling on it everyday. Credits the way Zimbabwe bowled. Ends by saying it was a very difficult track to bat on.

Zimbabwe skipper, Hamilton Masakadza, is disappointed how they let the game go after restricting South Africa to 100 for 7 at one stage. Reckons the bowlers bowled really well first up. Feels that their batsmen need more application. Reckons that the seamers were the ones who were threatening and he is disappointed to lose so many wickets to the spin of Imran Tahir. Admits they needed partnership which they did not get.

Earlier in the day, even South Africa found themselves in a spot of bother after losing seven wickets for just 101. But the comeback man, Dale Steyn, shone with the bat and bailed them out of a precarious situation. His maiden ODI half century and the record 8th wicket partnership with Andile Phehlukwayo helped the Proteas get a respectable total eventually. Zimbabwe's batting flopped but a word of praise for their bowlers. Everyone contributed and will be really disappointed with the way their batsmen responded. Stay tuned for the presentation...

To be honest, the visitors never got going in this run chase. They braved the early challenge by trying to survive the first spell of Steyn and Ngidi but post that it was a meek surrender. Imran Tahir was the chief tormentor as he bagged a 6-wicket haul (which included a hat-trick) and made a complete mockery of Zimbabwe's batting. The red team clearly lacked the required quality and there is a big question mark over their progress.

Zimbabwe were after a tricky target. 199 may not look too big but on a spicy pitch, it's definitely very difficult. To add to that, their fragile batting department and South Africa's potent bowling attack. The picture was more or so clear after watching the way Lungi Ngidi and Dale Steyn initiated with the new balls. They were smoking hot and were banging in thunderbolts. At one point of time, the track looked very dangerous for batting but then it settled down a bit once the bowlers with lesser pace came into the attack.

South Africa have thrashed Zimbabwe here to take an unassailable lead in the series. They are all smiles as Imran Tahir is leading them off the park. Handshakes near the boundary line. It has been a total domination and demolition.

OUT! SOUTH AFRICA WIN BY 120 RUNS! Tahir finishes with a 6-wicket haul. What a performance by the leggie! A long hop this time, on middle, Chatara goes deep inside the crease with the pull shot but fails to get enough power behind it. A straightforward catch for Steyn in the deep mid-wicket region. All over for Zimbabwe in this match and the series.
Loopy and on off, defended off the front foot.
Beaten! Spinning away from the batsman, Chatara tries to cut but misses.
Floated full ball on off, Tendai defends it by getting forward.
Turning back in with extra bounce. Chatara fails to defend and is hit high on the thigh pad.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

Grown up watching Donald Duck and Chip 'n' Dale. This is something like that. Comical. Donald Tiripano stays behind inside the crease to Dale Steyn. Expecting a short stuff but gets a not-so-short-one on leg. He jumps and defends it to short leg.
Darts in a length ball on middle and leg, Donald taps it down in front of short leg.
Backs away to a length ball on middle and works it to mid-wicket for a run.
Sharp delivery, in line of the stumps, Tendai defends it from the crease.
Snorter! A well-cooked bouncer, around the rib cage. Tiripano is hurried up as he tries to fend at it. The ball takes his gloves and flies over the keeper. A run taken.

Ha ha ha! It's fun to watch a number 11 facing a pace bowler of Dale Steyn's quality. Chatara just backs away expecting a bouncer. Then he finds that it's on a length around off, somehow touches it with his bat and pushes it towards covers. Runs to the other end more to save his life. Not sure Donald Tiripano will be too keen to face Steyn either.
Dale Steyn is back on. A short leg is in place. Time for some short stuff?
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
FOUR! Tahir bowls a rare bad delivery today. Drops it short outside off and Tiripano cashes in by slapping it through backward point for a boundary.
Misses the outside edge and the off pole by a whisker. A flipper probably, landing around off and skidding off the surface, Donald gets back to cut but misses.
Quicker and flatter on off, defended off the back foot.

Appeal for an lbw! Another wrong 'un which has not been read by Tiripano. He is forward in defense clueless about the spin. Gets hit on the pads, they appeal but the umpire remains unmoved. Maybe, missing leg.
FOUR! A googly on middle and leg, Donald leans forward to defend but it takes the inside edge and flies wide of leg slip for a boundary.
Good length delivery outside off, Tiripano plays it past the point fielder for one.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Width on offer outside off, it's nicely steered through backward point for a run.

Nearly drags it on! A length ball on off, shaping back in, Tiripano decides to shoulders arms but is late in withdrawing his bat. It collects the bottom edge and goes very closely past the stumps to the keeper.
Shortish and on off, punched from the crease to covers.
Appeal for an lbw, not given. A length ball angling into the batsman, Tiripano tries to defend but gets a big inside edge onto the pads.
Flighted and outside off, Chatara plays it down to point. 5 runs and three wickets off it, top stuff from the leggie.
Tendai Chatara is the last batsman for South Africa.

OUT! Castled! A fifer for Tahir, his third in ODIs. Jarvis with an attempted slog over the leg side. It's a googly and that could have been middled but Jarvis is way too early into the shot. He is already done with the swing of his bat as the ball arrives late and disturbs the timber. Just one more wicket left for South Africa to seal the series.
Shortish and on off, punched off the back foot through cover-point for one.
Three wides. Down the leg side, Tiripano fails to flick and it goes off the keeper's pads to fine leg. Two taken.
Flatter and on middle, turned in the gap on the leg side for a run.
Kyle Jarvis is the new man in.

OUT! HAT-TRICK FOR TAHIR! He is up and running in celebration. What a bowler! What a magnificent bowler! A googly is too good to read for the new batsman. It lands outside off, Mavuta has no idea about the variation as he plants his front foot forward in defense. But is of no use as the ball lands, turns back in, beats the inside half of his bat and lights the stumps. He's over the moon, this is the fourth occasion that a South African bowler has taken a hat-trick in ODIs.
Brandon Mavuta is in next.

OUT! Another batsman is trapped in front of the stumps. This is getting all too easy for South Africa. Tahir has three now. He fires in a quicker delivery, full and on middle, Moor plays down the wrong line, his bat is way wide of the ball as he takes a blow on his front pad. They appeal and Moor's innings is no more now. Dead duck.
A bouncer to end the over and Tiripano ducks under it.
Donald Tiripano is the new man in.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! They are now falling like a pack of cards! Length ball around off, Chigumbura tries to punch it through the off side but there is not a lot width to play the shot. The ball takes the outside edge and goes towards second slip. Hendricks there takes it easily.
Back of a length again on off, kept out.
On the shorter side outside off, Moor tries to push it but the ball stays a low. It hits the bottom half and goes down to third man for a run.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Back of a length around off, Moor keeps it out.
Andile Phehlukwayo is back on.
Elton Chigumbura walks in next with Zimbabwe staring down the barrel.

OUT! Now we know why Klaasen was so confident, Williams has nothing behind the line and he has been given his marching orders. Tahir gets his second and now Zimbabwe have half the side back in the hut. The googly got the better of Taylor and now it gets the better of Williams. He lunges and tries to defend but is beaten by the away turn. Klaasen takes the bails off and appeals. He seems very confident as the umpire takes it upstairs. The replays roll in and they show, Sean fails to drag his feet back in.
Have South Africa got another? Klaasen is very confident as he whips the bails off in a flash and appeals for a stumping. They have taken it upstairs. Williams is the man in question.
Another googly and it is once again picked. Moor punches it down to long on for a run.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
The googly, Moor picks it and works it with the turn to mid-wicket.
Another tossed up delivery but it is too full. SW, strokes it through covers for another one.
A low full toss on off, Moor pushes it down to long off for a single.
FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries! Once again Ngidi pays the price of over pitching. Williams strokes it through mid off and there is no stopping those. End of a good over for Zimbabwe. 9 from it.
FOUR! Lovely shot! Half-volley, Williams with a staright bat, times it through mid off and the ball races away.
Very full from around the wicket. Williams, who seems to be giving himself some room, jams it out towards mid off.
Good length again around off, Moor taps it towards the off side and takes a run. They need to keep the singles coming or the pressure will keep building.
Back of a length on off, the batsman guides it towards gully where the fielder makes a very good stop.
Hits the length around off, the batsman defends it towards covers.

Drinks! South Africa are right on top here and the pitch is playing all sorts of tricks. It is assisting the spinners and also the pacers. South Africa will look to continue in the same manner after the break. Zimbabwe on the other hand, need some sort of a partnership here but batting is difficult out there. One would expect the hosts' bowlers to run through the middle order as well or do we have a fight back in store?
Fires it very full on off, Moor times it down to long off for a run.
A little short on off, Moor gets back and keeps it out with ease this time.
This is what he should be bowling on this wicket! Slower through the air on off, it pitches and turns back in. Moor tries to defend but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Another shorter delivery, it is the quicker one. The batsman guides it to point.
Flatter on off, the batsman punches it to covers.
Down the leg side and it has been wided.

OHHH! Almost the 5th one there. Another googly outside off, the batsman lunges and tries to defend, leaving a big gap between bat and pad. The ball sneaks through and goes agonizingly close past the off pole.

Slightly over pitched, not a bad ploy though against a batsman who does not move ihs feet. However, he needs to bowl it a little wider of off. This is too close to the off pole. Williams strokes it to mid off.
Another shot way away from the body but luckily for Williams the ball whizzes past the outside edge.
Again on the pads, Moor tries to flick but misses to get hit on the pads. The ball rolls towards square leg. A leg bye taken.
BEATEN! Fuller in length around off, Moor's feet is glued to the crease as he tries to defend. Gets beaten.
Attacks the stumps again, Moor keeps it out.
Peter Moor is the new man in.

OUT! Another one bites the dust! The skipper, Hamilton Masakadza walks back and probably with him, he takes the hopes of Zimbabwe chasing this down. Two wickets in three balls for South Africa. On a length around off, this nips back in. Masakadza fails to account for the movement as he misses the ball while trying to defend. He is hit on the pads. The players appeal and the umpire once again raises the finger. Maybe a touch harsh as it could have gone down with the angle. No reviews though and Zimbabwe continue to slip further.
Flatter around middle, Williams keeps it out.
Sean Williams is the new batsman.

OUT! Taylor is out of here! Tahir starts his celebratory run and he was off even before the umpire raises his finger. That is how plumb it was. The googly does the trick. It is pitched around off and comes back in sharply. Taylor tries to defend but misses. He is hit flush on the front pad. The players appeal and the umpire raises his finger. Huge blow for Zimbabwe as their best batsman is walking back cheaply. They need another 156 in 217 with 7 wickets in hand.
FOUR! Good shot but a poor ball! Down the leg side, Taylor goes down on one knee and sweeps it fine through the leg side for a boundary.
Good bowling! It was tossed up and slower through the air. It was also the googly. Masakadza tried to defend it but got an inside edge towards square leg for a run.
A little too full on middle, Taylor eases it down to long on for a run.
Flatter on middle, Taylor works it towards mid-wicket.
Time for some spin! Imran Tahir is brought into the attack.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket. They pick up a single.
Another length delivery around off, Taylor plays inside the line and the ball whizzes past the outside edge.

Get in the gully fielder! Another ball goes uppishly through that region. Fuller in length around off, Masakadza tries to drive but the ball takes the outside edge and goes down to third man for a run.

Masakadza was a goner there! Luckily for him, Zondo misses. Taylor off the back foot pushes it towards cover. He wants a run, Hamilton responds. Zondo collects the ball, takes aim and fires a throw but misses by a whisker.
In the air... but no gully in place! Fuller in length around off, HM tries to drive but the ball takes an outside edge, goes uppishly through gully and down to third man for a run.
Just ahead of a length around off, Masakadza tries to push but gets it off the inner half towards mid-wicket.
On a length around off, Taylor looks to defend but the ball goes off the inner half towards mid-wicket.
Good batting! Masakadza pushes it towards mid on and gets to the other end.
Good length around off, Masakadza defends it out.
A little too straight this time, Taylor tries to flick but misses to get hit on the pads. The ball rolls towards the leg side and the batsmen take a leg bye.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

A huge shout! Andile bowls it on a length around off, comes back in sharply. Taylor tries to defend but the ball hits him on the pads and then on the helmet. The bowler asks the question but the umpire shakes his head. Height maybe.
A single to end! On the pads, worked around the corner for a run.
Not a good follow-up ball! Short and outside off, Taylor lets it be.
How has Taylor played that? Asks my colleague Milind. This was on a length around off, it stays very low. Taylor who is rooted to his crease, works it towards mid-wicket.
BEATEN! The outswinger around off, Taylor tries to defend but gets beaten.

That was a snorter. On the shorter side, the ball keeps rising and at a very good pace. Taylor tries to defend but the ball hits the top of the gloves and goes over the keeper towards third man for a couple.
Wide outside off, left alone.
Powerplay 2 has been signaled! Now a maximum of 4 fielders can be placed outside the ring. Also change of ends for Lungi Ngidi.
A dot to end a successful over. On off, the batsman defends it out.
Misfield and a couple! Back of a length on off, the batsman punches it towards cover. The fielder there lets it through and a couple is taken.
Another length delivery around middle, Hamilton works it towards mid-wicket.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
On a length again around off, Hamilton keeps it out.
Good length on off, MAsakadza keeps it out.
Brendon Taylor is the new man in.

OUT! What a catch! Andile Phehlukwayo, take a bow! Ervine departs in a way which not many would have thought. Watching him play till now, one would feel he would have been knocked over, caught at slip or maybe LBW. That is not the case. It is short and around off, Ervine goes for the pull but it does not come off the middle. It is still well hit towards mid-wicket. Andile there dives full stretch to his right and takes it with two hands. Brilliant. The South Africans are ecstatic and rightly so, they are top at the moment. 173 more needed.
Steyn goes fuller this time on off, Ervine lunges and keeps it out.
Like this one! However, he was ready for it as he gets on top of the bounce and guides it towards gully. The fielder fumbles but no runs conceded.

That stays very low! Excellently played by Ervine. It is on a length around off, does not take off after pitching. Ervine at the very last moment, gets his bat down in time. He gets a bottom edge to the slip fielder. Be ready for the one that takes off now Ervine.
He is really playing this shot well! Waiting for it and then guiding it down to third man for a single.
Another shot which could have been avoided! On a length around off, Masakadza could have left it but he goes after it. The ball stays a touch low and sneaks under his bat.
An off pace delivery to end the over. Full and outside off, Ervine goes for the full blooded drive but gets beaten.
On a length outside off, the batsman leaves it alone.
Well bowled but a loose shot that! On the shorter side outside off, the bounce gets big on the batsman. Ervine tries to play it away from his body but gets beaten.
Slower ball outside off, the batsman shoulders arms. Three dots to start Andile's spell.
Similar delivery to the last one, Ervine again keeps it out off the back foot.
Starts from around the wicket and angles it on the off pole. Ervine defends it off the back foot.
Andile Phehlukwayo is into the attack.
Another back of a length delivery, Masakadza stands tall and keeps it out. Good over for Zimbabwe, 8 from it.
TOP EDGE AND SIX! Zimbabwe will take it anyway. It is short and on middle, Hamilton goes for the pull but the ball takes the top edge and goes over the keeper's head. It carries over the fence.
Good batting! Drops this towards covers and scampers through for a run.

Brute! Back of a length on off, it takes off after pitching and also skids through. Ervine tries to defend but the ball hits him on the glove and falls beside the pitch. Steyn is really giving Ervine a tough time out there. He however, is surviving the tough period.
Another ball shorter in length. Ervine gets on top of the bounce and guides it to gully.
Shorter in length around off, Masakadza plays it well, he plays it late and guides it through short third man for a run.
Harmless delivery, wide outside off, Ervine leaves it alone.

Another delivery shooting off the surface and catching the batsman off guard. Masakadza gets into an awkward position as he fends at it and. The ball catches the outside edge but goes safely down to third man. They cross.
Shortish ball on off, defended from the back foot.
On a length around off, Hamilton defends it towards mid on.
A length ball around off, shaping back in, Masakadza gets half forward and just pushes it with good timing. Finds the gap through covers and takes a couple of runs.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Bumper! The batsman ducks under the bouncer at the last moment.
Some extra bounce again, around leg, Ervine stays back to play at it but misses and is hit on the gloves. Not carrying to fielders behind the stumps.

Lands it on a length and outside off, Masakadza doesn't commit himself here as he stays back and just nudges it to third man for a run. The uneven bounce on this surface will really test the batsmen. Pommie Mbangwa on air feels it's quite dangerous. Hmm...
Bouncer this time, at 145 kph, Hamilton ducks.
A length ball on off, Hamilton defends it this time off his front foot.

Nearly another wicket! Steyn is banging it in and generating excessive bounce to trouble the batsman. He lands it on a length around off and the ball shoots up. Masakadza is caught by surprise as goes back to fend at it. It catches the gloves and loops towards point. The fielder rushes forward and across but it falls in front of him.
Length delivery on middle, a little too straight, Masakadza works it in front of square leg for one.
Masakadza has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Pitches it up and outside off, Ervine drives wide of mid off and scampers across for a single.
Fuller and angling away from the batsman, Ervine drives but finds the cover fielder.
Full and just around middle, blocked out again.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Full and around middle, pushed towards mid on.
Nerves. CE tries to push it through the off side but the ball seams back in, takes the inside edge and goes past the leg stump towards fine leg. A single taken.
NOW, A GRUBBER. Steyn now dishes out a half volley, Craig tries to punch it through the covers but this one barely bounces!
And another! A good length ball on middle, Ervine looks to defend but the ball rises steeply and hits his gloves, then the helmet. OUCH. OUCH. OUCH.
That's a snorter! Steyn steams in and bowls a 145 kph short delivery around off. Ervine tries to shoulder arms but it hits him on the gloves before rolling behind. What a welcome to the new batsman.
Craig Ervine is the number 3 batsman.

OUT! Trapped in front! That's plumb. Dale Steyn is back and is looking in red-hot form. The speed gun shows 141 kph as Steyn serves a shortish length ball in line of the stumps. It nips back in a shade as Mire is caught on the back foot in an attempt to put bat on ball. Ends up playing down the wrong line and is thudded on the pads. They appeal and the finger is up almost immediately. First blow to Zimbabwe. 189 needed 287 balls.

Indecisive there, Hamilton. Sees a length delivery in the channel around off, Masakadza is in two minds, whether to play at it or leave, decides to do the latter but is late in removing his bat. It takes the bottom half of his bat and rolls towards the slip cordon.
This one is served too full and wide outside off, Masakadza lets it be.

FOUR! It's aerial and just finds the gap. Risky, very risky. Ngidi slants in a full ball on middle, Masakadza tries flicking it but fails to middle his shot properly. Gets it away off the inner half of the bat as it flies past the left side of the mid-wicket fielder. Tahir puts in a delightful chase from mid on, dives near the fence to pull it back but fails. Gets up and himself signals the boundary.
Straighter in line, turned away off the pads but straight to mid-wicket.
Play and a miss! Back of a length delivery outside off, holding its line, Masakadza goes back to punch it through the line but is beaten.
Angles in a full ball on middle, Mire flicks it in the gap at mid-wicket for a run.
Lungi Ngidi to operate with the second new ball. Two slips in place for him too.
Bowls it full around off, angling in, Masakadza gets on the front foot in defense.
Good length ball on off, the Zimbabwean skipper keeps it out safely to the off side.
Another straight drive albeit too straight and right back towards the bowler. Steyn gets down low and parries it behind towards mid off.

FOUR! Fine way to get off the mark in your 200th ODI. Steyn overpitches a bit and serves it on middle. Hamilton is on the front foot as he brings down a straight bat to meet the ball. Finds perfect connection and it screams away down the ground for a boundary.
Inside edge, there. Steyn angles it into the batsman, Masakadza tries to push it back but gets an inside edge onto the pads.

Starts with an outswinger. Lands it on a length around off and gets it to nip away a bit. Mire is on the front foot as he pushes it off the outside half of his blade to third man. Zimbabwe are underway with a single.

We're back for the run chase. 199 needed off 300 legal balls. Looks like a straightforward equation but if you bring the pitch into picture, it becomes a tough task. The Zimbabwean openers Solomon Mire and Hamilton Masakadza are out in the centre. The skipper is playing his 200th ODI and will be keen to get a win for his side today. The comeback man, who has already stamped his mark on this match with the bat, Dale Steyn, is ready to bowl with the first new ball. A couple of slips in place. Here we go...
